_comment: sim-robust-coupled-traction-v1: the bounded GPU proof config for the coupled outbound tow. The outbound_dock_to_bay tow stalled at x~=-3.93 (outbound1/warm9/warm10) NOT on geometry -- the lane is a straight y=15.25 pull, clear of the 797-obstacle static map at every recorded footprint, and the real controller follows it to goal in the kinematic model -- but on a PhysX drive-authority deficit: the coupled base cannot re-break-away from a near-stop, collapses into the measured_turn_radius low-speed latch, and faults coupled_no_progress (PR 201, working as designed). warm8/warm11 passed only by carrying entry momentum across the same spot. FIX = raise the drive-wheel normal force (caster lift) and drive force so the base re-accelerates from rest. Every key here is opt-in and backward compatible; absent => the prior behaviour byte-identical. The progress monitor (coupled_progress_escape) stays ON.
_integration_lane_steps: 1. Regenerate the mobile assets at caster_lift_m=0.03 (offline, NO GPU): python3 scripts/build_mobile_assets.py --source-urdf <shelfbot_gripper_isaac.urdf> --output-dir ~/datasets/twin-robot-in-store-boot-v1/mobile-casterlift030 --package-root <ros_share> --package-root ~/workspaces/shelfbot_newgripper --config <(echo '{"caster_lift_m": 0.03}'). This bakes the deeper caster recess into mobile_ur10.urdf + mobile_manifest.json; measure_transport still proves the home COM support margin on CPU.

2. Point the mission runtime config's 'mobile_manifest' at that new mobile_manifest.json, and merge the top-level 'wheel_drive'/'wheel_friction' keys and the 'navigation' switches below into the mission runtime config (do NOT hand-edit ~/datasets configs via this worker; the integration lane owns them).

3. Run the bounded couple+outbound proof on the warm8 lanes: run_mobile_restock.py --start-at couple --stop-after outbound (the exact outbound1 recipe), serialized through /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, HEAVY_MB=2500 if whispr holds VRAM, never --force.
4. Feed the run's nav-trace.jsonl to scripts/check_tow_traction.py --gpu-run <run-dir>: PASS iff the coupled outbound reaches the goal with no multi-second pin (the same gate warm8/warm11 clear).
_wheel_drive_note: config['wheel_drive'] feeds MobileController(drive_max_force, drive_damping) (physics_setup.assemble). Default None => 80 N.m / 100. BOTH physical levers are needed, not caster lift alone: the quasi-static budget (twin/traction.static_traction_budget) shows that at 80 N.m the per-wheel drive torque cap (2*80/0.16 = 1000 N available) BINDS below the friction limit even at wheel_friction 1.0 -- so raising caster lift alone cannot exceed it. Raising max_force 80 -> 200 N.m lifts the cap to 2500 N, unbinding it so caster lift's higher mu*N_drive then applies and the force-type velocity drive commands full torque through the re-breakaway transient instead of saturating. damping unchanged. Efficacy is the GPU bench.
_caster_lift_note: caster_lift_m lives in the mobile_manifest spec (baked into the URDF at build), not here -- see _integration_lane_steps step 1. 0.005 (the stuck runs) fixed the UNCOUPLED crawl (tracking 0.097 -> 0.988) but the heavier coupled re-breakaway still starves; 0.03 (the MobileSpec cap) fully unloads the fore/aft casters so ~all robot weight bears on the two drive wheels, maximising mu*N_drive. Clamp is enforced by MobileSpec.__post_init__ ([0, 0.03]).

_traction_budget._comment: Inputs for the quasi-static lever-direction budget (scripts/twin/traction.static_traction_budget). The CPU proof asserts the recommended config strictly dominates the stuck config in margin; absolute margin is not an efficacy claim (the real failure is dynamic re-breakaway, GPU-only).
